lifecycles._note: KMS transit-key CRYPTO lifecycle (C3 Tier-1 fix 2026-06-20; purpose confirmed 2026-06-23). Spine: (1) create RSA-2048 key (asymmetric, for sign/verify/encrypt/decrypt) -> capture key_id; (2) create AES-256-GCM96 key (symmetric, for hmac/datakey) -> soft-capture sym_key_id; (3) read-only list-managed-keys -> soft-capture managed_key_id for the PUT description step; (4) exercise all crypto ops; (5) teardown both keys. FIX (a): hmac+datakey now route to sym_key_id instead of key_id — RSA-2048 does NOT support hmac/datakey; CONFIRMED LIVE 2026-06-23: correct purpose is 'aes256-gcm96' (NOT 'aes-256' which was rejected with 400). Valid advanced key purposes: aes256-gcm96, ecdsa-p256, rsa-2048, aria. FIX (b): set-managed-key-description now uses managed_key_id soft-captured from list-managed-keys; account has 0 managed keys so placeholder remains unresolved and the step 4xx's, but if the account gains one it auto-upgrades to 2xx. All crypto/rotation steps are optional+grouped; a 4xx records coverage and isolates cleanly. encrypt returns a 'vault:v..' ciphertext soft-captured to feed decrypt/rewrap. sign returns a signature soft-captured to feed verify.

steps.name: create-sym
steps._note: Creates a symmetric (aes256-gcm96) key for hmac/datakey ops which require a symmetric key. RSA-2048 key above does NOT support hmac/datakey. Captures sym_key_id to route those ops below. CONFIRMED LIVE 2026-06-23: purpose='aes256-gcm96' is the correct enum value (API returns 400 for 'aes-256'). Valid purpose enums for key_type=advanced: aes256-gcm96, ecdsa-p256, rsa-2048, aria. Cleanup registered separately so it is torn down even if later steps fail.

steps.name: list-managed-keys
steps._note: Read-only GET: lists managed keys (system-managed, no create). Soft-captures first key id to feed set-managed-key-description below. Account may have 0 managed keys (empty list) — if so managed_key_id stays unresolved and the PUT step still fires against a placeholder (normalizes to * for catalog matching) and 4xx's. Same pattern as security-kms-managed-readonly lifecycle.

steps.name: datakey
steps._note: datakey requires a SYMMETRIC key (aes-256). Routes to sym_key_id captured from create-sym step. If create-sym 4xx'd, sym_key_id is unresolved and this fires against a placeholder (still records the endpoint, 4xx). See resource model: RSA-2048 does NOT support datakey.

steps.name: hmac
steps._note: HMAC requires a SYMMETRIC key (aes-256). Routes to sym_key_id from create-sym. If create-sym 4xx'd, sym_key_id is unresolved and this fires against a placeholder (still records the endpoint, 4xx). RSA-2048 key does NOT support HMAC — this was the root cause of prior 400s.

steps.name: set-description
steps._note: updatedescription (PUT /v1/kms/transit/{key_id}/description). Key body field is 'description' (KeyDescriptionRequest, doc request_example verified 2026-06-20). key_id resolved from create step. Tolerant [200,400,403,404] — state Active expected so 200; if key entered To_Be_Terminated 400/404 is acceptable.

steps.name: set-managed-key-description
steps._note: updatemanagedkeydescription: managed_key_id soft-captured from list-managed-keys step above. Account has 0 managed keys as of 2026-06-20 (GET /v1/managed-kms/transit returned count:0) so managed_key_id is unresolved — the path segment stays a placeholder (normalizes to * for catalog matching). Still fires and records the PUT /v1/managed-kms/transit/{key_id}/description endpoint. If the account gains a managed key, the soft-capture makes it 2xx automatically.

lifecycles._note: Light, READ-ONLY (no writes, no cleanup). Closes the static id-bound GET gap GET /v1/managed-kms/transit/{key_id} (showmanagedkey) by the list->soft-capture->show idiom (the same pattern iam-readonly-shows uses). managed-kms keys are SYSTEM-managed: there is NO create in the OpenAPI, so a synthetic id would be a guaranteed-404 dead read — instead we list the caller's managed keys (listmanagedkeys, GET /v1/managed-kms/transit, ManagedKeyPageResponse) and soft-capture a REAL key_id from the first item ($.keys[0].id), then show it. A bare account may have system-managed keys (real 2xx) or none (the segment stays a {placeholder} -> normalizes to the catalog '*' key so the GET is still CALLED and the endpoint statically reachable, 4xx-ing harmlessly). Both steps optional with tolerant [200,400,403,404]. Envelope grounded in data/api_docs.json: ManagedKeyPageResponse.keys[] -> ManagedKey.id (response_example $.keys[].id); the show returns ManagedKeyShowResponse{key:ManagedKey}. Does NOT touch the non-managed /v1/kms/transit create/delete (those live in security-kms-key + the crypto lifecycle above).

steps.name: list-managed-keys
steps._note: listmanagedkeys (zero required params; size/page/sort/name all optional). Soft-captures a REAL managed key_id from the first list item (ManagedKeyPageResponse.keys[].id). Drives show-managed-key below. Tolerant [200,400,403,404]: a bare account may have no managed keys (empty list) or be denied (403) — either way the show is still CALLED.

steps.name: show-managed-key
steps._note: id-bound read (showmanagedkey). Closes GAP-get-id for GET /v1/managed-kms/transit/{key_id}. Keys off the list-captured managed_key_id (a real id when the account has system-managed keys -> 2xx); if none, the segment stays a placeholder (normalizes to catalog '*') and 4xx's. Tolerant [200,400,403,404]; the GET is CALLED so the endpoint is statically reachable.
